moves.rationale: Rxd7 removes the key defender; if Black recaptures with Qxd7, Qb8+ creates a decisive back-rank attack with the bishop controlling d8.
Kxd7 removes White’s advanced rook for free. The king can safely recapture on d7, preserving Black’s queen and eliminating White’s only active invasion; Qxb3 merely trades queens after axb3.
Qb7+ keeps the black king exposed and is harder to neutralize than diagonal checks: it covers c8 and c6, while the bishop denies e7 and d8, forcing the king into a narrow set of squares.

Ke8 steps out of the queen’s seventh-rank check while retaining the coordinated queen, bishop, and rook. It keeps the king sheltered behind the e-file and avoids the exposed central route on d6; Black remains materially decisive.
Qb8+ renews the back-rank attack. The bishop controls d8 and e7; any queen interposition on c8 can be captured with check, leaving Black unable to trade queens.
Kd7 is the only safe reply to Qb8+: it leaves the queen’s eighth-rank line and avoids Qc8, which permits an immediate mating reply. Black keeps a major material advantage after escaping the check.
